chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Ismail ibn Jabir, who said:
I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), so he called for the meal, and they brought him thareed and meat. He called for oil and poured it over the meat, so I ate with him.

key_terms.ثَرِيد: Thareed: A dish consisting of bread soaked in broth or meat sauce.
key_terms.زَيْت: Oil (typically olive oil in this context).

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam eat in this hadith and how was it prepared?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the simplicity and modesty of the Ahl al-Bayt's diet, specifically the consumption of thareed, a dish of bread soaked in broth or meat. By pouring oil directly over the meat, the Imam demonstrates the permissibility of combining fats with solid foods, reinforcing the practical application of dietary laws in daily life. This account serves as a model of contentment with basic sustenance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on avoiding extravagance while enjoying lawful provisions.
